% A proof of Erdős Problem 689 (working note, April 26, 2026)
% Goal: autoformalize key statements into Lean 4 / Mathlib.

\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,amsthm,mathtools}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\newtheorem{proposition}[theorem]{Proposition}
\begin{document}

\textbf{Main theorem (Erdős Problem 689).}
For every sufficiently large positive integer \(n\), there exists an
assignment \(a:\{p\text{ prime},\ p\le n\}\to\mathbb Z\) such that for every
integer \(m\in[1,n]\),
\[
  \#\{p\le n\text{ prime}:\ m\equiv a_p\pmod p\}\ge 2.
\]

\textbf{Setup.} Fix a finite set \(S\subset\{7,11,13,\ldots\}\) of primes,
let \(W=\prod_{s\in S}s\), and choose nonzero residues \(b_s\pmod s\) for
\(s\in S\). For \(x\in\mathbb Z\) define
\[
  H_S(x)=\#\{s\in S:\ x\equiv b_s\pmod s\}.
\]

\textbf{Robust class.} A unit \(\pi\in(\mathbb Z/W\mathbb Z)^\times\) is robust if
\[
  H_S(\pi)\ge1,\qquad H_S(2\pi)\ge2,\qquad H_S(4\pi)\ge2.
\]
Let \(\mathcal B\subset(\mathbb Z/W\mathbb Z)^\times\) be the set of robust
classes, and \(\delta_S=|\mathcal B|/\varphi(W)\).

\begin{lemma}[Robust side-debt]
If \(P>n/5\) is a prime with \(P\bmod W\in\mathcal B\), and we set
\(a_P\) to any nonzero residue mod \(P\), then for every \(m\in[1,n]\)
divisible by \(P\), \(m\) is hit by at least two of: the parity class
\(a_2=1\bmod2\); the unchanged zero class mod 3; and the \(S\)-classes
\(\{b_s\bmod s\}_{s\in S}\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform half-residue marginals]
Let \(c_s\equiv2^{-1}b_s\pmod s\) and let
\(\mathcal C=\{A\bmod W: A\not\equiv c_s\pmod s\text{ for every }s\in S\}\).
For every \(A\in\mathcal C\),
\[
  \Xi_A^\infty
  :=\sum_{\substack{a\text{ odd }S\text{-smooth}\\ ar\equiv A\,(W)\\ r\in(\mathbb Z/W\mathbb Z)^\times}}\frac1{2a}
  =\frac12,
\]
\[
  H_A^\infty
  :=\sum_{\substack{b=2^j u,\,j\ge1,\,u\text{ odd }S\text{-smooth}\\ br'\equiv A\,(W)\\ r'\in(\mathbb Z/W\mathbb Z)^\times}}\frac1{2b}
  =\frac12.
\]
\end{lemma>

\begin{lemma}[Half-residue transport]
For every unit \(\pi\pmod W\) and every \(\sigma\in\{\pm1\}\),
\[
  \#\{A\in\mathcal C:\ A+\sigma\pi\in\mathcal C\}=\prod_{s\in S}(s-2).
\]
\end{lemma>

\begin{theorem}[Surplus margin]
With \(\beta_*=\tfrac12(1-\tfrac35 e^{-2})\) and \(\delta_*=1/(\beta_*+3/5)\),
if \(\delta_S>\delta_*\) and \(\delta_S^{-1}-\tfrac35<\beta<\beta_*\), then
\[
  \Delta:=(\beta+\tfrac35)\delta_S-1>0.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Cleanup ledger]
Set \(N=|A_S(n)|\), \(|\mathcal R(n)|=(\tfrac45\delta_S+o(1))N\),
\(|M_n|=((\beta-\tfrac15)\delta_S+o(1))N\), and exceptional-token count
\(E_S(n)=o(N)\). Then for sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
  |\mathcal R(n)|+|M_n|\ge |A_S(n)|+E_S(n).
\]
\end{proposition}

\textbf{Goal.} Autoformalize the main theorem statement and the four
intermediate statements (robust side-debt lemma, uniform half-residue
marginals, half-residue transport count, surplus-margin theorem, cleanup
ledger) into Lean 4 / Mathlib. Do not attempt full proofs — produce
well-typed statements with correct quantifier order and the appropriate
Mathlib types (Nat, ZMod, Finset, Filter.atTop).

\end{document}
